Hey there Leandro. 

Interesting case. It’s shady. I’ll try to explain what I noticed. 

From the driver’s side: his last finished order was on 18/12/20. Then he comes back and all his recent orders were with this same passenger where he rejected all other requests that came from legit clients. The trips themselves, look weird. The client never had a history of long rides and now all of sudden is doing these long ones. All in the same day, one after the other, driving back and forth. Trips finished in different destinations, without a single complaint from the client about the overcharges. All (except the first) with a 5 euro tip, which is the max allowed in Lisbon. Rider also had 195.55€ and 195.53€ failed preauth. Bunch of signs pointing to them trying to cash out the card. Looks like someone got a hold of the rider’s account and is trying to get paid. Honestly, my advice here is to keep the account blocked. My bet is that these payments will turn into chargebacks. However, I wouldn’t make a call on the Fraud side alone. All I pointed out here are indicators of fraud, there is no concrete evidence so far. Payments are too fresh, so they’re still good. The only evidence we have is that the driver had suspicious behavior and did a bunch of repetitive pre-arranged rides, not sure if this is enough for us to withhold his payment. Please escalate this to the local ops and see what they think. I would leave the call with them, to unblock or not.

Bolt Market Romania users have a MOV (minimum order value) of RON 30 for orders they place. If their order is, let’s say, 24 RON. they pay a minimum order fee of 6 RON (30 - 24). This is communicated to them at check-out. 

At the moment, we can play with the MOV threshold and minimum order fee/penalty as per how our product is set-out. 

We have a number of users which shop 2 packs of cigarettes which are roughly RON 45 which is beyond our MOV (RON 30) and also have free delivery (which we want to keep on doing for a couple of month). Problem is that tobacco products have fixed selling proces as per legislation so we are making roughly 3.75% margin on them. This means we are in fact losing money on each tobacco-only order since we cannot cover courier fee and other direct/indirect expenses from the margin we gain from the product. 

A potential walk-around from Product team would be to exclude Tobacco products from MOV calculations while also limiting minimum order fee/penalty. Let’s say we have the scenario in which the user wants the 2 packs of cigarettes at RON 45; in this case his MOV would be RON 0 (as cigarettes are excluded from the MOV calculation) so the minimum order fee/penalty would kick-in. which we limit to RON 14. It would be the decision of the client if one drops the order, is willing to pay the RON 14 (minimum order fee/penalty), or tops up the order with regular products worth RON 30 (MOV) to pay no fee/penalty while also enjoying free delivery. 

Our concern on the above is whether there are some legislative implications around this indirect restriction. Tobacco would be the only products with this exclusion behaviour and might be indirectly considered that we are trying to restrict them in some way. Still. We also have troubles communicating this exact exclusion to customers, so this could also lead to some legislative implications perhaps for cases where users would not pay attention to this, end up with the penalty of RON 14 and start complaining to Consumer Protection Agency. What do you think?

The only course of action that can realistically be recommended from our side is to dissuade possible attempts to change the delivery type as it cannot be done properly from the product side. The process would be very complicated for CS in most cases, and even then there is a  chance that it would not have been done properly since the order cannot be succeeded without a courier being assigned to the order, and most requests for this type of change come precisely because the courier has not been assigned.

Agents would have to either wait and keep refreshing the order page to catch the moment when the courier is assigned so that they don’t start driving towards the restaurant and losing money they won’t get from us OR they would have to assign a random courier and then succeed the order. Both options would require outgoing contact to the courier to explain to them what happened + manual deductions.

{noformat}#!/bin/bash
cp /lib/systemd/system/etcd.service .
cp /etc/default/etcd .
sudo systemctl stop etcd
mkdir etcd_backup
sudo etcdctl backup --data-dir /dev/shm/etcd/default etcd_backup
sudo rm /etc/default/etcd
sudo apt remove --purge etcd etcd-client etcd-server -y
sudo apt update -y
sudo apt install etcd=3.3.27-1 -y
cp etcd /etc/default/
cp etcd.service /lib/systemd/system/
chown -R etcd:etcd /dev/shm/etcd/default
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl start etcd{noformat}

A few insights and ideas:

* Ideally, we would like to move away from the custom blocks placed by the CS. Why?
** With BQS rolling out, there should be left almost no other reasons for driver blocks, thus, there is no need to have a possibility to block drivers with a custom reason; other reasons can be added as proper reasons to choose
** When custom blocks are used, there is no way to get a good overview on driver blocks. ~85% of manual driver blocks placed by CS agents are custom blocks. Manual blocks placed by CS constitute ~20% of all the manual blocks placed. Thus, we can’t have a proper overview of the blocking reasons for ~17% of all the drivers blocked. This is a difficulty in understanding how to optimise our work with drivers and keep the needed level of supply on markets.
** Messages used for custom blocks may or may not be clear and informative for drivers, thus, causing a bad driver experience (e.g. the blocking message “Please contact Support team” does not contain any information on why the driver’s account is blocked). Messages are added manually by the agents placing the blocks and we can’t always influence the way they structure blocking messages.
* Ideally, we would like to move away from CS having to manually block drivers (except HP cases). Why?
** CS is not to take care of the supply quality or overall supply in the market. As well, CS agents don’t have the full picture to make a decision to block the drivers for behaviour issues, for example. There is a problem with CleverTap ingestion process on our side [~accountid:5fbb62502730d800768e5f8c] 
Here are some steps how ingestion process can be tested.

# Get a list of all ingested files with “Notification Sent” events that we received from CleverTap on S3 storage:
{noformat}aws --profile dataeng s3 ls s3://taxify-clevertap/ | grep "Notification-Sent-20220118" > notification_sent_20220118.txt{noformat}

# Copy all the ingested files locally to `notification_sent` folder:
{noformat}while read -r line
do
	aws --profile dataeng s3 cp "s3://taxify-clevertap/$line" "./notification_sent/$line”
done < notification_sent_20220118.txt{noformat}

# Now unzip all the files in the directory:
{noformat}gzip -d *{noformat}

# Now we can read files, make search through them with different command line tools. But we don’t need to do it. If you open even one file out of many, for instance `1624605291-1642510800-Notification-Sent-20220118-0-1.json`, you see that it contains around 600K different “Notification Sent” event, which is already more than 1K.

So far I noticed one issue with ingestion process. We parse export files wrong. The file format is described [on this page|https://docs.clevertap.com/docs/data-export-to-aws-s3#file-name-format]:
{{<export request id>-<timestamp of the export run>-<event name>-<yyyymmdd>-<file index>-<database-id>.json}}

In Spark job we {{timestamp of the export run}} field when we need to read {{yyyymmdd}} as event date. But that does not explain why we have only 1K events. Further investigation is to be done yet.

Hi [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] \! Before providing advice on this I think there are several aspects here that need discussing.  

The meaning of account deletion is different from the request of deleting personal data. However, account deletion should trigger the deletion of personal data (after a period which is set beforehand in the retention schedule). 

*a) FO request for deletion of the account*

Account deletion should mean that the account can not be retrieved - so the account would be archived (not closed). FO should have the right to ask for the deletion of their account, however this does not automatically mean that all data should also be deleted. 

If the account is deleted, the personal data should be deleted based on the retention period set. 

Questions for [~accountid:5fa118a781b2880078eb0e6f] 

# If the FO asks for the deletion of their account → does this constitute as the termination of the agreement (also what agreement)? Is there a notice period actually necessary? How do we see the “account deletion” from legal perspective. 

2. What happens to driver accounts after the fleet owner account is “deleted”?

*b) Request for deleting the personal data.* 

It is not possible to request deletion of personal data separate from deleting the account. 

If the account is deleted, the personal data should be deleted after a reasonable time period - based on retention schedule. 

It is clear that right now we don’t have the retention schedule for data processed in the fleet portal. But in general it should follow the same logic that:

* all account data (including FO details and driver details) is retained for 3 years after account deletion - for possible claims, disputes arising from the agreement with the FO 
* data necessary for accounting purposes is retained for 7 years
After these periods, personal data will be permanently deleted. 

*Other questions:*

# Verification of identity - if we communicate with the FO by using their provided e-mail, then account deletion request should be deemed sufficient if it comes from that e-mail as well. 

Let me know your thoughts and if I missed something here.

Unfortunately, we cannot just add new issue tags as the whole logic behind issue labelling now is different: 

* the new tags show the problem from the user’s perspective (issue tag = how the user describes his/her problem) and do not indicate potential tech/root causes of the request as in most cases it’s rather difficult to identify it only within one request because more complex analyses are needed.
* The previous system was way too defragmented, it didn’t allow us to see the full scale & impact of some difficulties the users faced on a global scale. 
* The system doesn’t only have a different range of tags but also any list of issues we have now or add/change is visible to our users. It means that the issue tag list isn’t “internal” but also forms the list of topics users choose before contacting us and the tags aren’t market-specific. Unfortunately, that also influences any decision re the issue tag changes as due to that, the list can’t be very long or super detailed.

I understand that this logic is completely different but it gives us a chance to investigate the users' issues in a more data-driven way than it used to be before.

Hi [~accountid:61445ec9ea73af006a785f36] 

Regarding your question about whether it is possible to remove the _standard value commission_ from the Special Terms, please see our conclusions below: 

The thinking behind adding a specific commission percentage to the Special Terms was: 

a) We do not want this to be public - hence not in the T&Cs;
b) For large fleets our goal is to set up an elaborate scheme and establish dependency on KPIs, so a single percentage would not work and therefore we need to specify it in a detailed agreement; and
c) For small fleets where commission is clear and set as a simple percentage, in fact it is not necessary to have it in Special Terms if that it is the business preference. However, our T&Cs say in section 5: 

_“The amount of the Bolt Fees will form part of the Special Conditions of the Fleet, provided to the Fleet Partner by email, via Bolt Apps, Fleet Partner Account Bolt or other relevant means._ *_Fleet Partner acknowledges that the Bolt fees may change from time to time. Bolt will send to the Fleet Partner a prior notification_* _\[15 days] before each change.”_ 

In short, you can unilaterally change the standard commission set out in the Special Terms by notifying it by email.  

Bearing in mind that to change the commission percentage it is not necessary to modify the Special Terms but only to communicate the change to the fleets by a simple email, I would leave it as it is now. But of course it’s a business decision.

Should you have any further question, please do let me know.

Many thanks \!

From the local legislation and further action:

_Note\! Specific to Estonia, legislation regarding found items can vary._

The general rule is that if the item is worth more than 50 EUR, we have to notify the police about the found item.

By the current legislation, we could destroy the found items if we have publicly announced the found items and the cost of storing/keeping the found items outweighs the possible value of the item. 

So, I think we can recommend the drivers to take the following actions (1 & 2 are also applicable for us if we have stored any items):

# Current items stored, valued more than 50 EUR - notify the police; we will not become the owners. After notifying and handing over, we can free up some space in the office.
# Current items valued less than 50 EUR and have been in storage for more than 1 year - we have become the owners and can decide further action (destroying, selling etc). 
# Future found items valued more than 50 EUR - Police is informed and the found item is handed over to them for further processing;
# Future found item valued less than 50 EUR - will be held in accordance with the TnC and destroyed after 30 days have passed. If no TnC change is made, we can decide the further action by evaluating the possible cost of organising the sale/action versus the possible selling price. If there is no point in selling, the item can be destroyed.
# Fast spoiling goods (foodstuff etc) - by the current legislation they should be _publicly_ auctioned off. But if storing and auctioning exceeds the value of the item, we can destroy it.

As we are processing items valued less than 50 EUR, you can make the preliminary estimation - every minute spent on the lost item generates about 0,50 EUR costs per person.

Hey, thanks for raising this. I have set up a call for today to discuss this further. In order for the privacy team to assess these proposals fully, we would already need a pretty detailed plan of what would be proposed as solutions (the product fixes). However, certain privacy principles should be kept in mind which we could discuss already in the call.

*Sharing data on alleged/confirmed sexual offenders with competition (we have already initially discussed the idea with Uber and FreeNow) to ensure they will be effectively blocked from all the platforms.  perhaps it would be possible to share data of a vehicle that the ride was provided with?* probably sharing data on the vehicle would just be a safeguard but it would still probably constitute personal data since the vehicle can quite easily be linked to the individual. 
in order to share such data, we would need to know in detail what data exactly we want to share to assess what could be the legal basis for sharing the data. it is probably going to be a legitimate interest but for that to work we need to carry out a balance test which would show how the benefits here outweigh the intrusion of drivers privacy. 
also, we would need to share as minimal data as possible to serve its purpose and make sure from our part that the data is accurate. probably the accuracy part is one of the key elements - how do we make sure we are sharing data about actual sexual harrassment cases and single out false accusations. 
if sharing personal data with third parties, then also data protection agreements need to be put in place.
we also need to then be transparent about such processing and make amendments to our privacy notices about us possibly sharing such data with other RH companies. 



If it is going to be widespread data sharing in big volumes, then due to the sensitivity of the data, privacy team probably needs to carry out a data protection impact assessment

My colleagues Laurent (Ride Hailing Country Manager) and Marc (Regulatory / PP) have been discussing extensively with taxi operators/drivers as well as the Belgium government (Bruxelles Mobilité) and it seems that both the taxis and the government makes an interpretation of the Brussels Order that means that the price indicated by the taximeter is in fact the maximum price - but not the definitive, imposed price - i.e. it can be decided that the final price could be lower than the price shown by the taximeter.

You might recall that clause 4.6bis of the Providers T&Cs specifically refers to article 43 of the Brussels Order:
_"EN: When You provide taxi services within the scope of Chapter II of the Brussels Ordinance of 27 April 1995, You must use a taximeter pursuant to article 37 of the Brussels Order of 29 March 2007 on taxi services and car rental services with driver (the “Brussels Order”) and_ *_the Fares shall be determined pursuant to the tariffs provided in article 43 of the Brussels Order._*_"_

[https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/24R6TOQGWJpDtIOgZo7Ng4/96fc2304d9de42017723a6d44feadb7c/20220106_-_BE_Providers_T_C_-_FINAL_version__EN_.docx.pdf|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/24R6TOQGWJpDtIOgZo7Ng4/96fc2304d9de42017723a6d44feadb7c/20220106_-_BE_Providers_T_C_-_FINAL_version__EN_.docx.pdf]

Indeed, article 43 of the Brussels Order details the taximeter tariffs. However, the government seems to agree with the fact that article 43 needs to be read in conjunction with article 31 - which would mean that the price indicated by the taximeter is only the maximum price that can be charged by taxis:

"_Il est interdit aux chauffeurs : (...) 3° de réclamer un prix supérieur à celui indiqué au taximètre, sauf suppléments spéciaux ou tarifs forfaitaires décidés par le Gouvernement en application de l'article 29, alinéa 1er, de l'ordonnance_".

Laurent explained that taxis want to be more competitive and align their prices on LVC prices, and therefore the Business is keen on lowering prices from the taxi category.

Could you please therefore advice on the below:

* Do you agree that if we read article 43 in conjunction with article 31, it only means that the taximeter indicates a maximum price - not a set, definitive price and therefore the Bolt Fares for Brussels taxis could be lower than the taximeter prices?

* In order to offer Fares lower than the taximeter for Brussels taxis, can we rely on the existing wording under clause 4.6bis - or do we have to amend it to specifically refer to articles 43 and 31 or perhaps can we just adopt a broad wording, such as:

_"EN: When You provide taxi services within the scope of Chapter II of the Brussels Ordinance of 27 April 1995, You must use a taximeter pursuant to article 37 of the Brussels Order of 29 March 2007 on taxi services and car rental services with driver (the “Brussels Order”) and_ *_the Fares shall be determined pursuant to the Brussels Order_*_."_

_"FR: 4.6bis. Lorsque Vous fournissez des services de taxi dans le cadre du chapitre II de l'Ordonnance Bruxelloise du 27 avril 1995, Vous devez utiliser un taximètre conformément à l'article 37 de l'arrêté bruxellois du 29 mars 2007 relatif aux services de taxi et aux services de location de voitures avec chauffeur (l' "Arrêté Bruxellois ") et_ *_les Prix sont déterminés conformément à l'Arrêté Bruxellois._*_"_

* If we need to amend clause 4.6bis of our T&Cs, can we make that change without having to notify each driver / operator individually (for the ones who are already been onboarded and have already received a copy of our T&Cs) - perhaps by relying on clause 14.1 and the fact that such change would not be material if in fact it reflects the government's and the taxis' understanding of the prices as determined by the Brussels Order?

* I don't think the Passenger T&Cs would be impacted by such change to the ProvidersT&Cs but would be grateful if you could please confirm this.

Response from OC Belgium, 16 Feb:

_We confirm that we agree with the interpretation of the Brussels Government and that article 43 of the Brussels Ordinance only set maximum prices._

_In fact, the competence to set taxi fares was originally a competence of the Belgian Federal State and the State had set the fares in a decree of 11 January 2002 "fixing the maximum prices for transport by cab". Consequently, at that time it was obvious that the rates defined by the legislation were maximum rates._

_Then, the competence was transferred to the Regions and the Brussels government's decrees do not say it expressly, but what is defined is still maximum fares, the drivers being free to propose lower prices (article 31 of the Brussels Decree only prohibits prices higher than what is indicated by the taximeter)._ 

_As article 43 of the Brussels Order only set maximum prices for the taximeter, there is, in our opinion, no need to modify art. 4.6bis of the T&Cs to apply lower prices. Actually, pursuant to art. 4.6bis of the T&Cs, BOLT only requires the Providers not to charge prices in excess of those set forth in article 43 of the Brussels Order when they operate taxi services in Brussels._

_However, if you wish to modify the T&Cs in order to clarify (e.a. by indicating, like you suggested, "_*_the Fares shall be determined pursuant to the Brussels Order")_*_, you can indeed use article 14.1 of the T&Cs to operate the limited modification you mentioned  without notification as it has no consequence for the Providers. You could also take the opportunity to put the second "Prix" in art. 4.6bis in fine, in lower case._

_Passengers T&Cs do not address the question of the fare structure so we confirm that these T&Cs are not impacted by this discussion._

By definition, a _child_ is “a young human being below the age of puberty or below the legal age of majority” - this differs from country to country, so we should not limit this by adding a specific age to the definition.   

Events in which a driver is reported to be making advances on underage individuals (and the individual is reporting to be clearly distressed by it and hence have seemingly not consented to anything) should be logged as “*Driver Commits Paedophilic Actions*” as is being done now.

If you have any examples of recent cases where this EC has caused confusion or issues, I’d be happy to have a look to see what could be clarified.

It seems like the driver sharing their phone number with the rider, and vice versa, would be classified under Inappropriate Behaviour.

{{Rider Inappropriate Behaviour}} is a Regular Event, which means that we should log the event as soon as we have all of the details from the reporting user and inform the reported user of the action taken after the investigation with the resolution. Therefore we will not add this extra step to this SOP. 

{{Driver Inappropriate Behaviour}} is a Significant Event where we contact both users before making a consequential decision. We could add this in that we can ask the rider to provide us with the phone number the driver provided them with and then compare it with Admin data, but there are a couple of concerns before we can do so: 

* How can you confirm that the number belongs to the driver? They may have several phone numbers if it doesn’t match with Admin. This would cause inconsistencies in the process as we can not confirm the phone number actually belongs to the driver and then asking for the phone number in the first place would not help us with the investigation. 
* Will the agents then perform a cross-check with the driver’s Change Log each time a report comes in? The drivers change their phone numbers often. This will add extra steps to the investigation.

Hi [~accountid:5e9a112618b8ed0c0f776390] \!

Processing biometric data means processing special category of personal data. Before taking such equipment to use, conducting a data protection impact assessment is mandatory as the activity is likely to result in high risk. 

There is no technical nor data protection information in the agreement (e.g. what are the infosec measures, where is the data stored and transferred, what are the roles and obligations of the service provider and Bolt regarding data processing etc). 

Also, the only legal basis to process biometric data is consent. As consent is voluntary and in employment relationship the consent isn’t deemed given voluntarily, then an alternative mean for timekeeping must be provided at the same time. Hence, the use of magnetic cards or any other similar alternative must still be provided for the employee. 

As there are actually a lot of risks regarding using this system, then do we have maybe other less intrusive ways to conduct the timekeeping? 

Liis

Hi Mike\! No problem. What we call friend reports is basically getting weekly data for driver earnings from competitors so we can then compare to our metrics (e.g. rides per hour, earnings per hour, bonuses, etc).

The way it works is that we organise 30 min f2f sessions with these drivers, we ask for their feedback and then we ask if they drive with other platforms to. If yes, then we ask them if they would be willing to share how much they earned last week or last 2 weeks with Uber. Once they agree, we take a screenshot/photo of their earnings dashboard. We centralise it in a private folder on our drive and then we collect all the data in a spreadsheet where we run our calculations. 

Historically we haven’t been consistently doing these sessions but we were establishing relations with drivers that were sending us this data in exchange of a £50 bonus on a monthly basis.

With the project we are looking at, we want to offer the £50 Sainsbury’s Voucher for each attendant.

*11. Suspension and revocation, and appeal options (s13(6), s16, 17, 22, 25 and 26 1998 Act)* 

A PHV driver's licence may be suspended or revoked by the Licensing Authority if the licence holder: 

* has been convicted of an offence of indecency, violence or dishonesty; 
* where the Licensing Authority is no longer satisfied that the licence holder is fit to hold a PHV driver's licence, or; 
* where the licence holder failed to comply with any condition of the licence or other obligations imposed on him by the 1998 Act. 

In the event of suspension or revocation of a PHV driver‟s licence, the Licensing Authority is required to give notice of the decision to the licence holder which sets out the grounds for the decision. The suspension or revocation of the licence takes effect only at the end of the period of 21 days beginning with the day on which the suspension/revocation notice is served on the licence holder unless an appeal is lodged, see below. In the interest of public safety, the Licensing Authority may decide to suspend or revoke a licence with immediate effect. Where this is the case, the Licensing Authority will include a statement of this in the decision letter and the reasons for the immediacy of the decision. The suspension or revocation of the licence then takes effect when the notice is served on the licence holder. 

*A licence holder whose PHV driver's licence has been suspended or revoked may appeal to the Magistrates Court within the 21-day period against the decision to suspend or revoke the licence.* With the exception of an immediate suspension or revocation of a driver‟s licence, where a licence holder whose PHV driver's licence has been suspended or revoked exercises his right of appeal, the decision to suspend or revoke the licence will not be effective until the time for the appeal has been determined or withdrawn. Upon suspension or revocation of a PHV driver's licence, the licence holder is required to return the licence to the Licensing Authority within the period of 7 days after the suspension or revocation takes effect. Failure by a licence holder to return a licence or disc upon suspension or revocation is punishable upon summary conviction to a fine up to penalty level 3 and in addition, daily costs of up to £10.

*Answer to Q1*. No, we cannot favor Bolt Market in a way described above if we are not subsidizing other grocery providers from our pocket. Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (“*TFEU*”) states that it is prohibited to apply dissimilar conditions to equivalent transactions with other trading parties, thereby placing them at a competitive disadvantage. Although TFEU applies to the trade between EU member states, this principle is also reflected in the local legislation of the most EU member states. This means that the prohibition to place other trading parties at a competitive disadvantage applies also to the trade within local markets of the EU member states.

Of course, this matter shall be analyzed separately depending on each market, since additional requirements may apply on the basis of local laws. For instance, in some markets agreements, actions or decisions of minor importance are allowed.

Nevertheless, we are entitled to apply differentiated treatment with regard to our Bolt Market stores to some extent as long as Bolt Food does not hold a dominant position on a specific market. In order to do that, according to European Union law, other grocery providers on the Bolt Food platform need to know that Bolt Market is subject to differentiated treatment by our Bolt Food platform. This means that we need to outline the framework of differentiated treatment in our T&C’s. Each case of differentiated treatment needs to be assessed separately and with respect to a certain market.

*Answer to Q2*. Yes, it is acceptable, provided that:

* Bolt Food is not a dominant player on the market,
* Bolt Food T&Cs reflect that sales data of our providers is accessible to our employees.

Nevertheless, it would be advisable to avoid using Bolt Market competitors’ sales data for Bolt Market operations. Even if we are not risking any fines while being non-dominant on the market, it will be bad PR for our company. In addition, the moment when the company becomes dominant on the market is not always clear. If there will be any proof of our employees using sales data of providers operating on Bolt Food platform to our advantage while we are dominant on the market, these actions may bring serious antitrust infringement claims.

Amazon is a dominant player on the US market. Therefore, it has faced some serious antitrust allegations due to the access to the sales data of third parties operating on the Amazon platform.

_The sale of cigarettes to consumers is regulated by the Romanian Fiscal Code, which imposes a ban on selling to consumers at a price higher than the retail price declared to the Ministry of Finance by the producer/importer of the cigarettes._

_Nonetheless - and this is not practically tested - Bolt may reasonably argue that, if the minimum order fee is passed through to the fleet, this is entirely the cost of the delivery service and not retained by Bolt as part of its price. ***

We looked into the insolvency matter. In particular we researched the case on [https://www.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de/|https://www.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de/|smart-link]  which is the official portal where the German insolvency courts make publications required by the German Insolvency Code (_Insolvenzordnung_, *InsO*). Please find attached the result of our search for the provider’s name on the platform and the respective publication (“öffentliche Bekanntmachung”). Although the documents are in German you will notice the name of the provider and the case no. In case you notice differences between the court order provided by the preliminary insolvency administrator and the notice published in the official portal, please note that the latter may be published in excerpt.

Thus, we were indeed able to verify that *there has been a motion to open insolvency proceedings against TEO Taxi und Mietwagen GmbH* (the “*Debtor*”) and that the competent court has ordered preliminary measures to secure current funds remaining available to the creditors. +One of these measures is the appointment of a+ +_preliminary_+ +insolvency administrator: Frank Brachwitz,+ [+Karl-Heinrich-Ulrichs-Straße 24, 10785 Berlin+|https://www.google.com/maps/search/Karl-Heinrich-Ulrichs-Stra%C3%9Fe+24,+10785+Berlin?entry=gmail&source=g] +- the sender of the letter you received+.

The (preliminary) insolvency administrator also offers information on the case on his website: [Gläubigerinformationsystem von Pluta|https://www.glaeubigerinformation.de/p/345160/start]. You can switch the website to English in the upper right hand corner.

In addition, *the court has ordered that the Debtor's debtors (third-party debtors) are prohibited from making payments to the Debtor. They are requested to make payments only to the preliminary insolvency administrator* (Section 23 para. 1 sentence 3 InsO).

*Thus, until further notice,* +*you must not make direct payments to the Debtor*+*.*

*The preliminary insolvency administrator should provide you with account data of a special separate account for the purposes of the (preliminary) insolvency administration soon*.

In addition to this, the insolvency administrator asks to be provided with the Debtor’s Bolt-account log in data. Since the court order does not provide for a duty to provide information for third parties other than credit institutions, you are under no obligation to hand over the login data. Without having investigated this further, +*we would advise to not provide the login data for possible data-privacy law implications*+.

***

→ +Based on our local counsel advice, I would advise to:+

# *Stop any payment to TEO Taxi und Mietwagen GmbH*
# *Ask the preliminary insolvency administrator to provide you with account data of a special separate account for the purposes of the (preliminary) insolvency administration*
# *Refrain for now from providing the insolvency administrator with the Debtor’s Bolt-account log in data*, as this is not mandatory and could have data privacy laws implications.

Hope that helps but please let me know if you have any further questions on this.

[~accountid:6125f1f3fc55090071ffb944] 70% have used both cash + inapp (52k); 27% only in-app (20k); 3% (or 2k drivers) haven’t attempted to pay at all. In this time period 3.7k cash-blocked drivers churned so roughly half of them are making payments at least once before churning which is quite interesting as at least they’re trying to use our product to make a living (potentially 1.7k of these drivers have left us due to being unhappy about being blocked)

Checking the numbers per country we can confirm the previous findings. In South Africa 89% drivers used in-app but only 8% used cash. Alarmingly, if the driver had been cash-blocked in South Africa, 10.5% (~1.6k) didn’t attempt to make any payments. So we can say in ZA ~80% of drivers are continuing to drive to repay the debt.

In Nigeria & Kenya, cash payments are more popular: Nigeria - 97% used in-app & 76% used cash (2.5% / 1k drivers didn’t pay at all) hence we can say ~20% of the drivers are driving to repay the debt; Kenya - 93.6% used in-app & 93.8% used cash (4.8% / 900 drivers didn’t pay at all) hence we can say only ~1.4% of the drivers are continuing to drive to repay the debt.

As a general rule, in case of an infringement, a right holder may request from the infringer to cease using the work and claim damages for unauthorised use. However, we consider these risks quite low. This opinion is based on the available information that a) the Work is based on open source software elements combined in a new way after Aleksandr has left Yandex; and b) the possibilities for third parties to find out exactly which solution is used by Bolt are very limited. 

If the decision is made to use Work in the Bolt app, a separate agreement on transfer or licence of Work should be signed between Bolt and Aleksandr. The agreement should be signed before the actual use of Work in the Bolt app. In addition to transfer or licence terms, the agreement should include Aleksandr’s representation that Work does not infringe any third party rights. 

Please let me know if you have decided to include Work in the Bolt app, and on what basis (transfer to Bolt or licence), and I will draft a suitable agreement. 

For the sake of completeness, as the use of open source software in the Bolt app requires that copyright notices and permission notices are included in the Bolt app, a list of open source software and licences should be published in the app (I understand that open source software list used by Bolt is a wider issue and does not cover this specific case alone).

Adyen response:

Thank you for reaching out to us\! In short, yes you can refuse transactions when the liability shift didn't occur. 
To do this, you can set a risk rule to to increase the fraud score for transactions that don't have the liability shift. When a transaction has a fraud score of more than 100, the transaction is automatically refused. You can do this under *Risk* > *Risk profiles*

You can trigger the check on transactions where:


* Full authentication of the cardholder has not taken place: Triggers if the 3D secure server can not authenticate the cardholder. Full authentication is stricter and always requires a (Y)-Authenticated response. The issuing bank may grant a liability shift without an authentication. 
* 3D Secure liability shift has not taken place: Triggers if no liability shift has occurred for the selected transaction types. This does not always require full authentication by the user, for example, for automated authorizations performed by the issuing bank.


More info on this can be found [here|https://docs.adyen.com/risk-management/configure-standard-risk-rules/consistency-rules?utm_source=bo_live#liability-shift-status] and more info on setting up risk rules in general can be found [here|https://docs.adyen.com/risk-management/create-and-use-risk-profiles].

1. The issue *_I didn't receive the cancellation fee_* is to be used for cancellation fees only. Issue description is: _Driver didn't receive the cancellation fee for order, which they believe they should have received it for._

I have added another issue *_Total ride fare was too low_* to the process for missing wait fee scenarios in [🔒 Driver reports cancellation fee or wait time fee was not charged|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360013304500--Driver-reports-cancellation-fee-or-wait-time-fee-was-not-charged]. The description for this one reads: _Driver claims parking, toll or any other additional fee was not added to the fare or driver feels that the total fare was too low (inclusive of technical reasons eg. GPS issues, starting the trip too late or ending the trip too early etc.)_

Let me know if you think anything would remain unclear after this change. : - )

2. *_I have an issue with my payout:_* _Driver didn't receive a payout for any of the reasons or they received less than expected_

*_I have an issue with my driver balance:_* _Driver is having an issue with their balance not reflecting the correct expected amount eg. unresolved price review, tips not appearing in balance etc. Not to be confused with missing bonuses._

{quote}Such as, if the driver reports of a specific trip, is this also included in the payout matter? Or is this matter already related to driver balance/total ride fare was too low?
{quote}

An example would be useful here as issues are to be tagged based on user’s POV/description of their issue. For example:

* If they report a specific trip that ended up being cheaper than expected: *_Total ride fare was too low_*
* If they are missing a payout or their payout amount was inaccurate: *_I have an issue with my payout_*
* If they are reporting an inaccurate driver balance, for example a pending (PR) trip is not reflected (not payout): *_I have an issue with my driver balance_*

So, to help you decide:

* I would always follow the descriptions of the issues (as they are set by the Supportability team who own the issue tagging logic)
* Tag based on user’s POV/exact description of their issue.

Hi [~accountid:6102798be6e6f80071b2fadb],

*Search of pickers' bags*. We cannot search pickers' bags at the end of the shift. There are two exceptions for this rule: 1) picker has consented to bag search or 2) court ruling allows us to do so.

*Cameras*. In regard to the cameras, our privacy counsel [~accountid:609f85c547ba02006fe1b9c3]  has previously given the following advice. If the video surveillance is put in place for security reasons then this is okay under the legitimate interest legal basis under GDPR. It is okay to use video surveillance to prevent, detect and investigate theft and property damages or threats to the safety of the employees working in the premises.  

It is prohibited to use video surveillance system for any other purpose, such as to monitor the work of employees or their attendance. +This means that there should be no live monitoring on the employees for the purpose of checking the performance of their duties.+

# *Positioning the cameras*

The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms etc.

# Retention period

All personal data processed must have a retention period. No personal data should be kept indefinitely, so a proportionate and reasoned retention time must be set for keeping this data. 

Retention period must be determined depending on the purpose why this data is being collected. 

Data can be stored for no longer than it is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected (e.g the market practice for storing this data is 30-60 days, but can be shorter or longer depending on the need). 

After the retention period, recordings must be deleted automatically (overwritten by new video footage). 

# Warning signs of video surveillance

*3.1 Position of the warning sign.* 
It is obligatory to install warning signs on the premises where video surveillance is carried out. The information should be positioned in such a way that the data subject can easily recognise the circumstances of the surveillance before entering the monitored area (approximately at eye level). 

*3.2* *Content of the warning sign.*

The warning sign/sticker can be as following:

Camera picture/”we have video surveillance”

_Purpose: Safety of people and property_
_Legal basis: legitimate interest_
_Controller: Bolt Operations OÜ_
_Detailed information:_ [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/|smart-link]  or QR code to the page

Hi Hedda\!

*TL;DR*: the policy can be implemented in Sweden but we need to be careful on how we package and present it to not break anti-discrimination legislation. 

*Challenge*
Under mandatory Swedish law, absence from work due to parental leave and sick leave counts towards the employees length of service within a company. Further, the scope of the policy as described in this ticket, where it is +expressly+ stated that absence from work due parental leave and/or long term sick leave does not count towards length of service (for the purpose of eligibility for additional paid leave) would be deemed discriminatory under Swedish law (both on the grounds of parental leave and disability, depending on the reason for sick leave). 

This said, employees on parental leave are generally not entitled to retain bonus benefits which are based on work performance as such payments are viewed as a form of “retroactive salary” under Swedish law. Therefore, if eligibility for the additional leave would instead be given as a form of bonus based on the total amount of days worked *(i.e. eligibility for the additional paid leave would be based on work performance)*, this would instead most likely be viewed as a form of retroactive benefit under Swedish law (and would therefore likely be permitted). I believe that the same reasoning should also apply in respect of employees on sick leave.

*Solution/Conclusion*
A performance based bonus is ok. It needs to be packaged as e.g. ’if you work X days over a 5 year period you’re entitled to the bonus’ rather than saying that people on a sick leave or parental leave are excluded. This should be the global packaging/presentation, not a Swedish carve-out.

Please note that you’re also not allowed to discriminate against part-time or fixed-time employees. To avoid doing just that part-time or fixed-time employees should also be allowed to take part of the bonus policy – on a _pro rata_ basis, of course, to not put the part-time or fixed-time employees in a better situation than the full-time employees.

Dan

We need to add a default value for the fields {{order_scheduled.arrive_at_client_at}} and {{order_flexible.expires_at}}

The DB servers has the {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}} disabled. This means that {{TIMESTAMP}} columns following the first one, must: *Explicitly allow* {{NULL}} *or have a* {{DEFAULT}} *value.* Otherwise the automatic {{DEFAULT}} is {{'0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'explicit_defaults_for_timestamp';
+---------------------------------+-------+
| Variable_name                   | Value |
+---------------------------------+-------+
| explicit_defaults_for_timestamp | OFF   |
+---------------------------------+-------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec){noformat}



The fields {{order_scheduled.arrive_at_client_at}} and {{order_flexible.expires_at}}:

* aren't the first {{TIMESTAMP}} type,
* they are declared as {{NOT NULL}}
* and it has no explicit {{DEFAULT}}

So MySQL automatically declared as {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}}.

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/server-system-variables.html#sysvar_explicit_defaults_for_timestamp]

 

With this, we hit another restriction:

The {{sql_mode}} in DB servers has includes {{NO_ZERO_DATE}}, which means that the {{DEFAULT '0000-00-00 00:00:00'}} is not a valid value.

{noformat}mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'sql_mode';
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Variable_name | Value                                                                                                                              |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| sql_mode      | IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION |
+---------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec){noformat}

_Please refer to_ [MySQL 5.7 Reference Manual :: SQL Mode :: NO_ZERO_DATE|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.7/en/sql-mode.html#sqlmode_no_zero_date]

 

An attempt to create the table as described above will fail with the following error: {{ERROR 1067 (42000): Invalid default value for 'arrive_at_client_at'}}

 

Possible solutions are:

# Enable {{explicit_defaults_for_timestamp}}, which requires further analysis, as the database servers are shared hosts and the change will apply to other services.
# Explicitly declare a default non zero value i.e. {{occurred_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP}}.
# Explicitly declared with the {{NULL}} attribute.

Hei, I reread your question and to be honest the system has always been designed like this. Regardless of the driver seeing the destination or not, they'll never know how many (if at all) trips they’ll receive which start in, go through or end in the Congestion Charge Zone during their shift. That’s why Bolt adds Congestion Charge fee (£1.50) to all trips which start in, go through or end in the Congestion Charge Zone so if the driver makes 10 trips during their day they’ll already have covered the fee for that day. If they do 20 trips, then they get 15 GBP extra that day. Therefore, long term it’ll balance out and this is the way it works. 

So that feature will not help the driver, what they essentially want to do is to fully avoid the ULEZ area, which in turn might affect their activity score etc negatively. As I said, one day maybe they’ll be a bit short but another day they’ll get more than they should essentially.  

If the feature of seeing rider destination is activated in UK, it’ll be announced in relevant channels. But this won’t be the fix for this specific question.

{code:sql}USE taxify_reseller;

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS migrate_reseller_order_on_demand;

DELIMITER $$
CREATE PROCEDURE migrate_reseller_order_on_demand()
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_min_id, v_max_id BIGINT;
    DECLARE v_batch_size INT DEFAULT 200;

    DECLARE v_sleep_cnt INT DEFAULT 0;
    DECLARE v_sleep_after INT DEFAULT 1000;
    DECLARE v_sleep_time INT DEFAULT 5;

    SELECT MIN(id), MAX(id) INTO v_min_id, v_max_id FROM taxify_reseller.reseller_order;
    SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, v_batch_size;

    WHILE v_min_id <= v_max_id DO
        INSERT INTO order_on_demand (reseller_id, reseller_order_id, city_id, order_id, search_category_id, created, last_update, state)
            (SELECT reseller_id,
                    id                        AS reseller_order_id,
                    city_id,
                    order_id,
                    filter_search_category_id AS search_category_id,
                    created,
                    last_update,
                    CASE
                        WHEN order_state IS NULL THEN 'cancelled'
                        WHEN order_state = 'waiting' THEN 'searching'
                        WHEN order_state = 'searching' THEN 'searching'
                        WHEN order_state = 'cancelled' THEN map_order_try_state_for_cancelled_order(IFNULL(order_try_state, ''))
                        WHEN order_state = 'active' THEN map_order_try_state_for_active_order(IFNULL(order_try_state, ''))
                        WHEN order_state = 'finished' THEN map_order_try_state_for_finished_order(IFNULL(order_try_state, ''))
                        WHEN order_state = 'no_driver_provided' THEN 'no_driver_found'
                    END AS state
            FROM reseller_order
            WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL AND is_backfilled = 0 AND id >= v_min_id AND id < v_min_id + v_batch_size)    
        ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE reseller_id = VALUES(reseller_id),
                                reseller_order_id = VALUES(reseller_order_id),
                                city_id = VALUES(city_id),
                                order_id = VALUES(order_id),
                                search_category_id = VALUES(search_category_id),
                                created = VALUES(created),
                                last_update = VALUES(last_update),
                                state = VALUES(state);

        SET v_min_id = v_min_id + v_batch_size;
        SET v_sleep_cnt = v_sleep_cnt + 1;

        SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, 100 * v_min_id / v_max_id AS completed, v_sleep_cnt, v_sleep_after;

        IF v_sleep_cnt > v_sleep_after THEN
            SELECT CONCAT('Sleeping ', v_sleep_time, ' sec');
            SELECT SLEEP(v_sleep_time);
            SET v_sleep_cnt = 0;
        END IF;
    END WHILE;
END;
$$
DELIMITER ;{code}

{code:sql}USE taxify_reseller;

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS migrate_reseller_order_flexible;

DELIMITER $$
CREATE PROCEDURE migrate_reseller_order_flexible()
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_min_id, v_max_id BIGINT;
    DECLARE v_batch_size INT DEFAULT 200;

    DECLARE v_sleep_cnt INT DEFAULT 0;
    DECLARE v_sleep_after INT DEFAULT 1000;
    DECLARE v_sleep_time INT DEFAULT 5;

    DECLARE i INT;

    SELECT MIN(id), MAX(id) INTO v_min_id, v_max_id FROM taxify_reseller.reseller_flexible_order;
    SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, v_batch_size;

    WHILE v_min_id <= v_max_id
        DO
            INSERT INTO order_flexible (reseller_id, reseller_order_id, search_category_id, payment_method_type,
                                        payment_method_id, ready_for_dispatch_at, expires_at, token, created,
                                        last_update, state)
                (SELECT ro.reseller_id,
                        ro.id                                                             AS reseller_order_id,
                        rfo.search_category_id,
                        rfo.payment_method_type,
                        rfo.payment_method_id,
                        IFNULL(rfo.scheduled_at, rfo.created)                             AS ready_for_dispatch_at,
                        DATE_ADD(IFNULL(rfo.scheduled_at, rfo.created), INTERVAL 24 HOUR) AS expires_at,
                        rrslt.token,
                        rfo.created,
                        rfo.last_update,
                        CASE
                            WHEN ro.order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'dispatched'
                            WHEN rfo.state = 'cancelled' THEN 'cancelled'
                            ELSE 'scheduled'
                            END                                                           AS state
                 FROM reseller_order ro
                          INNER JOIN reseller_flexible_order rfo ON ro.flexible_order_id = rfo.id
                          INNER JOIN reseller_ride_sms_link_token rrslt ON ro.id = rrslt.reseller_order_id
                 WHERE ro.is_backfilled = 0
                   AND rfo.id >= v_min_id
                   AND rfo.id < v_min_id + v_batch_size)
            ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE reseller_id           = VALUES(reseller_id),
                                    reseller_order_id     = VALUES(reseller_order_id),
                                    search_category_id    = VALUES(search_category_id),
                                    payment_method_type   = VALUES(payment_method_type),
                                    payment_method_id     = VALUES(payment_method_id),
                                    ready_for_dispatch_at = VALUES(ready_for_dispatch_at),
                                    token                 = VALUES(token),
                                    created               = VALUES(created),
                                    last_update           = VALUES(last_update),
                                    state                 = VALUES(state);

            SET i = v_min_id;

            loop_label:
            LOOP
                IF i > v_max_id OR i > (v_min_id + v_batch_size) THEN
                    LEAVE loop_label;
                END IF;

                UPDATE reseller_order
                SET requested_stops = (SELECT JSON_ARRAYAGG(JSON_OBJECT('address', address, 'lat', lat, 'lng', lng))
                                       from reseller_flexible_order rfo
                                                inner join reseller_flexible_order_stop rfos on rfo.id = rfos.flexible_order_id
                                       where flexible_order_id = i)
                WHERE flexible_order_id = i;

                SET i = i + 1;
            END LOOP;


            SET v_min_id = v_min_id + v_batch_size;
            SET v_sleep_cnt = v_sleep_cnt + 1;

            SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, 100 * v_min_id / v_max_id AS completed, v_sleep_cnt, v_sleep_after;

            IF v_sleep_cnt > v_sleep_after THEN
                SELECT CONCAT('Sleeping ', v_sleep_time, ' sec');
                SELECT SLEEP(v_sleep_time);
                SET v_sleep_cnt = 0;
            END IF;
        END WHILE;
END;
$$
DELIMITER ;{code}

*Mastercard - Revised standards for the Decline Reason Code service for card-not-present transactions in the EEA Countries, United Kingdom, and Gibraltar*

Mastercard is creating a new decline reason code for authorisations. This service will help ensure issuers properly use transaction decline codes, and provide merchants and acquirers better insight on the decline. Today the issuers often use a default or generic decline reason code (such as response code 05- Do Not Honor). The Decline Reason Code service is limited to card-not-present (CNP) declines, excludes mail and telephone order. Mastercard will map a subset of sensitive decline reasons on behalf of the issuer into three categories. Three new decline response codes will be introduced: Life Cycle (response code 79), Policy (response code 82), and Fraud/Security (response code 83).  

h3. What you need to do:

_You need to be aware that you will stop receiving certain decline codes that are not technical or financial in nature for CNP declines. Some examples of such decline codes include_

* 04 (Capture Card)
* 14 (Invalid Card Number)
* 41 (Lost Card)
* 43 (Stolen Card)
* 54 (Expired Card)
* 57 (Transaction Not Permitted)
* 62 (Restricted Card)
* 63 (Security Violation)

Please find attached the *reply* we have received from *Sintra*.

 

In short, Sintra municipality considers that: (i) the activity of a dark store shall be considered retail trade (and thus shall be subject to the Legal Regime of Commerce); (ii) the establishment and operation of dark stores shall be subject either to a mere prior communication or to an authorization, depending on the case; (iii) dark stores shall be installed and operate in premises licensed for _commerce and services;_ (iv) those premises shall be located _preferentially_ in _economic activity spaces_ (article 96 of the Sintra Urban Master Plan Regulation – “SPDM”), without prejudice to the principle of compatibility of the uses foreseen in article 90 of the SPDM.

 

Basically, the Sintra municipality conveyed the same ideas as the other municipalities, except in what regards item (iv). What Sintra states in this item implies that, whenever dark stores are installed in areas (_spaces_) that are not qualified as _economic activity spaces_ (e.g., _residential spaces_) a particular attention must be given to the compatibility of the actual use of the premises _vis-a-vis_ the type of space where the premises are located.

 

In our case, the premises of Rua Professor Agostinho da Silva, 26C, 2725-530 Mem Martins, seem to be located in a _residential space_ (type 1). Pursuant to article 94 of the SPDM, _residential spaces_ may host other uses deemed compatible with the _residential use_, such as those related with _economic activities_ (including _commerce_ _and_ _services_), provided that a number of conditions are met, namely: (i) the other use do not call into question the functions of the main use; (ii) the other use does not affect traffic and parking, or provoke loading and unloading movements that impair the conditions of use of public areas.

In conclusion, provided that the premises are indeed licensed for _commerce / commercial_ use, the external counsel’s opinion is that the premises meet the requirement set out by Sintra Municipality.

*************************** 1. row ***************************
           Procedure: migrate_reseller_order_scheduled
            sql_mode: IGNORE_SPACE,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY,STRICT_TRANS_TABLES,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,NO_ZERO_DATE,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION
    Create Procedure: CREATE DEFINER=`debian-sys-maint`@`localhost` PROCEDURE `migrate_reseller_order_scheduled`()
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_min_id, v_max_id BIGINT;
    DECLARE v_batch_size INT DEFAULT 200;

    DECLARE v_sleep_cnt INT DEFAULT 0;
    DECLARE v_sleep_after INT DEFAULT 1000;
    DECLARE v_sleep_time INT DEFAULT 5;

    SELECT MIN(id), MAX(id) INTO v_min_id, v_max_id FROM taxify_reseller.reseller_order;
    SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, v_batch_size;

    WHILE v_min_id <= v_max_id DO
        INSERT INTO order_scheduled (reseller_id, reseller_order_id, city_id, delayed_order_id, search_category_id, arrive_at_client_at, created, last_update, state)
            (SELECT reseller_id,
                    id                        AS reseller_order_id,
                    city_id,
                    delayed_order_id,
                    filter_search_category_id AS search_category_id,
                    arrive_at_client AS arrive_at_client_at,
                    created,
                    last_update,
                    CASE
                        WHEN order_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'dispatched'
                        WHEN order_state = 'cancelled' THEN 'cancelled'
                        ELSE 'scheduled'
                    END AS state
            FROM reseller_order
            WHERE delayed_order_id IS NOT NULL AND is_backfilled = 0)
        ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE reseller_id = VALUES(reseller_id),
                                reseller_order_id = VALUES(reseller_order_id),
                                city_id = VALUES(city_id),
                                delayed_order_id = VALUES(delayed_order_id),
                                search_category_id = VALUES(search_category_id),
                                arrive_at_client_at = VALUES(arrive_at_client_at),
                                created = VALUES(created),
                                last_update = VALUES(last_update),
                                state = VALUES(state);

        SET v_min_id = v_min_id + v_batch_size;
        SET v_sleep_cnt = v_sleep_cnt + 1;

        SELECT v_min_id, v_max_id, 100 * v_min_id / v_max_id AS completed, v_sleep_cnt, v_sleep_after;

        IF v_sleep_cnt > v_sleep_after THEN
            SELECT CONCAT('Sleeping ', v_sleep_time, ' sec');
            SELECT SLEEP(v_sleep_time);
            SET v_sleep_cnt = 0;
        END IF;
    END WHILE;
END

* In a *Services Agreement*, the employees are _not_ Bolt’s temporary workers, they remains Triangulu’s employees and the relations should be between Bolt and Triangulu. In this case, most of the obligations remain on Triangulu's side  Bearing in mind that the services are “Driver Verification” and “Document Verification”, DLA confirmed that in their view, a Services Agreement is the right option for our needs here - and as mentioned before, in such case, it is advisable that Triangulu assumes the day to day control of the activities of Triangulu Staff.

Under a Services Agreement, the Contractor (i.e. Triangulu) must be liable for all the consequences of the services and the management of the employees should be kept by Triangulu (without prejudice of Bolt’s control of the activities).

e.g.: The warranties mus be given by Triangulu and not by the employees: The Agreement is between Bolt and Triangulu. Thus, the responsibility for performing correctly the services is solely form Triangulu. Bolt as no relation with Triangulu’s employees and Bolt can not demand the employees directly.

* a '*Contract for the use of temporary work*' would require a completely different agreement. This would allow Bolt to _hire_ temporary employees such as drivers or other internal staff to conduct activities.

→ Considering it was agreed from the beginning that we would enter into a *Services Agreement*, it means that we cannot accept most of the changes requested by Triangulu. *Common themes in these issues:*

* _CS waiting for instructions from OPS:_
** Currently, CS agents usually report such issues to the OPS team via Slack and wait for their instructions
** OPS usually just ask CS to contact the previous user
** *How it should be:* OPS should be contacted only when we basically have all the details and need to figure out a solution (after which user we started receiving reports of the messy van, what did the user potentially at fault say)
* _CS check the past users only in two cases:_
** after OPS ask them to find the previous user, or 
** when CS are already aware and have seen/handled multiple reports about the same van and issue
** *How it should be:* CS should already find these details and get the story from the user who’s potentially at fault
* _The users who are potentially at fault react negatively and decline it was them:_
** Most often, users, when asked about the van’s condition when they rented it, say it was alright and that the trash isn’t theirs
** If CS inform them about the potential fine, these users may take it as an insult and/or threaten, or have already gone to social media about this
** OPS and Bolt generally want to avoid such media outbreaks in fear that users portray such events as Bolt penalising users without much explanation or hearing them out
** It is likely that CS avoid mentioning fines to such users because most commonly they take it as an insult and threaten, or already have taken matters to social media
** *What can be done:*
*** The purpose of renting a van is for transporting certain goods - so how likely is it that a user didn’t even use the trunk part of the van during their order and didn’t even check the trunk? (why would a user rent a van if they don’t intend to use it for transporting something? It is highly likely that the user is just lying)
*** CS should always hear out the previous user, even if OPS want to issue a fine right away (it’s not the fine that has to be issued right away - it’s the contact with the potential user at fault that has to happen immediately)
*** The T&C, Penalties and Additional Fees clearly state that the user is responsible for the vehicle’s state, and the app also encourages to leave feedback on the vehicle at any stage of the order - so we’re covered there
*** Any response from our CS should be carefully crafted to not accuse the user and also make them aware of the ‘rules’ without being blunt
*** The fine amount is 69 Eur - it is not the end of the world even if the user who is charged is not at fault and is not happy with it

*Conclusions:*

* CS must find the potential user at fault and contact them immediately to hear their side of the story - but the response has to be carefully crafted so that we don’t sound accusatory and uninterested to hear their story
** The response should be very carefully crafted also to not give the user any details that they could turn against us in case they decide to take the matter to social media

Here are my propositions for the process update for handling reports of our VW Crafter vans being left full of trash:

* Currently, CS agents usually escalate the issue to OPS and wait for their instructions - which usually are to find and contact the previous user:
** While the new process update for dirty vehicles includes leaving comments in Admin and contacting the user only at the 3rd occurrence, I believe resolving the trash in our VW Crafters is an urgent issue requiring immediate contact with the user after which we started receiving the issue reports (otherwise, the next users cannot use the trunk to transport their goods)
** When receiving a report with the VW Crafter trunk having lots of garbage of furniture, I think it’s safe to assume that people don’t just _forget_ stuff like that - most likely, they intentionally leave it there.
** The CS task should be to immediately look for other vehicle reports of the same issue and find out who is the user after which we received the first report - it is likely that this was the user at fault (at least we can safely assume that based on what our T&C say, the user being responsible for the vehicle during their order and reporting anything that’s wrong with the vehicle)
* We should always hear the accused party and actually give them time to clean out the car - that way we don’t come across as accusatory or blunt. We can inform the user of the situation and potential consequences, and help them book the van to go and clean it out to avoid the resulting fine. This
* Only when they refuse to do that, we can assume that the user doesn’t want to take responsibility for the vehicle’s state when they finished the order - and escalate to OPS to issue a fine and have Fleet OPS clean out the car.
* The fine for a dirty vehicle is 69 Eur - even if we end up accusing the wrong user, the fine is in my view low enough to accept losing the user if they react negatively to the fine. Such customers cause unnecessary hassle for Drive, and it can be a very good lesson for the user to not assume that not knowing/checking will free them from the responsibilities. We have a similar approach with users who speed or do other highly suspicious or illegal activities during their orders.
* While we’ve had bad publicity cases (the sofa one, for example, with the user taking the matter to a Facebook group), they were bad because we made our mistakes, too. With that said, if we hear out the potential user at fault, give them time to sort out the issue and inform them what happens if they don’t, then it’s safe to charge them the fine, even if they intend to go public with this.
** If we have a clear conscience that we did our best to help the user and at the same time do everything we can and have to to ensure good service quality for all users (including the ones reserving the vehicle with trash inside), then it’s ok even if they go to social media.

Paparazzi - full of byte code hacks and relies on layoutlib (which is used by Android Studio to render previews). It does support latest API level and I didn’t manage to do that. But they have a nice visual diff between the two images.

Facebook screenshot-tests-for-android - works on an emulator and does not support the latest API level as well. The main issue is with scoped storage. This library is more CI-oriented because I didn’t find a convenient way to run a single test directly in Android Studio. All operations are done by invoking the corresponding Gradle task. But tests themself are more stable because run on an emulator which is closer to a real device than the layoutlib rendering.

[Avito Screenshot Testing|https://github.com/avito-tech/avito-android/blob/develop/subprojects/android-test/test-screenshot/src/main/java/com/avito/android/test/screenshot_test/test/BaseScreenshotTest.kt] - the open-source project from my previous job. * Studied internal calls involved in {{/internal/GetFlatMenu}} flow via {{timedAsync}} monitors - deployed in prelive and tested on some heavier menus
* In terms of queries, the main pressure points are the following:
** {{MenuItemTagTable::getMenuItemTagsForMenuIds}}
** {{MenuItemTable::getMenuItemsOfMenu}}
*  Study showed that tag retrieval queries {{scales approximately linearly wrt menuItems}}. Specifically, if you have N tags on for each menu item, {{getTags}} will take approximately N times longer than {{getMenuItems}}.
** This linear dependency can be seen in the picture below which shows the evolution of max durations of calls in the {{getFlatMenu}} flow  with same number of items (7k) and increasing number of tags: {{0, 1, 3, 7 tags per item}} -> 3 calls for each configuration.

!image-20220227-224358.png|width=1092,height=318!

*Conclusions*: 

* Query investigation via pmm did not show any clear possible quick wins atm. Speed increase could be gained with additional indexes, however we’d be more inclined to save space and remove indexes instead of adding them, by relying more on {{stable_id}} .
* Further optimization efforts should be clearly directed in the area of {{scaling the tags retrieval for menus with many tags}}. 
** [Menu Vision First steps|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3634168196/Dec+2021+-+Big+Menus+-+Menu+vision+first+steps#Process-in-parallel-events-for-stable-availability-(safely)] doc describes 2 more optimizations that can be done in this area, but require more time. Hey [~accountid:619f7f77c15977006a86dc43] , currently the process looks like this:


h3. *Where to find Bolt Market missing items reports*

All Bolt Market missing items reports will come to your local Slack channel (e.g. #bolt-market-refunds-ee).

Make sure to have the post notifications for this channel turned on.

----

h3. *How to handle Bolt Market missing items reports*

When you see the missing items report, aim to refund the order within one hour. 

If you’re working on a report, react to it with a ✅ emoji. This way, you can avoid having multiple agents working on the same issue.

----

h3. *How to refund Bolt Market missing items*

Each Bolt Market missing items report consists of the following information:

* Order reference
Provider ID
Missing item(s) name
Quantity

To refund the item(s):

* Find the order in Admin Panel by searching the order reference
Scroll down to _Basket items_ section
Check the price of the missing item(s)
* Proceed with adding a refund:
** Type: partial
Comment: list the missing item(s) here 
Ticket #: since there is no ticket, put “/”
Actor at fault: Bolt
Amount: the value of the missing item(s) + compensation (small amount if one item was missing, medium amount if more items were missing)
* Once the refund has been processed, no further action is required

----

h3. *What to do if the wrong order reference is provided*

* Search the provider ID in Admin Panel > Delivery > Orders
Look for the order manually based on the time when it was created and the provided order reference
If you are unable to find the order, escalate the case to your local BM OPS by tagging them in the Slack post 



CS will not be informing anyone about these refunds. If you want to be kept in the loop, request  from the TL to be added to your local refunds channel.
